item.text: This is a large Guava-style multi-module Java repo with a clean worktree. I’m going to look for a low-risk internal duplication or complexity hotspot that already has focused tests, so the refactor can be verified without touching broad public API behavior.

item.text: One promising area is `com.google.common.io`: `ByteSource` and `CharSource` each have skip-based counting code and extensive tests. I’m reading those implementations now to see whether there’s a small internal cleanup that doesn’t change semantics.

`CharSource.length()` has its own skip loop, while `CharStreams` already centralizes related stream operations. I’m checking the existing `skipFully` behavior before moving anything, because this code has subtle EOF and zero-skip behavior.

I found a concrete refactor candidate: give `CharStreams` the same internal “skip up to N” helper pattern that `ByteStreams` already has, then reuse it from `CharSource.length()` and `CharStreams.skipFully()`. I’ll add focused tests around a reader whose `skip` returns 0 even though reads can still make progress, which is the edge case this consolidation handles better.

The tests already use small custom readers in this package, so I’ll keep the new coverage local to `CharStreamsTest` and add one `CharSourceTest` assertion that `length()` benefits from the shared helper. Next step is a small patch in `CharStreams`, `CharSource`, and those tests.

I’m going to edit the character stream path only: extract a package-private `CharStreams.skipUpTo(Reader, long)`, route `skipFully` and `CharSource.length()` through it, and add regression-style tests for readers that cannot skip but can read.
The patch is in place. I’m checking the diff and then I’ll run the focused Guava IO tests so any subtle stream behavior issues show up immediately.
